questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Always start your motorcycle with the transmission in neutral. Most motorcycles have a light on the speedometer that shows when the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: The best way to stay out of trouble while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
Ride at speeds faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Always scan the road ahead of your motorcycle. Watch for hazards early so you can react before you reach them.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning the correct braking technique is important for safe riding.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
Not worry about the oil and grease buildup.
Search for the lane with the smallest amount of oil and grease buildup.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of the lane. This strip is usually narrow, so you can ride to the left or right side and still stay in the lane.

questions.question: If using saddlebags to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
Unevenly distribute weight into the saddlebags.
Place as much weight as possible into one saddlebag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
questions.explanation: Put equal weight in both saddlebags. If one bag is heavier than the other, the motorcycle may drift to one side.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to be out of the way of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake is ineffective on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Make smooth movements when speeding up, shifting gears, turning, or braking.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in ______ of a lane.
questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil drippings and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting gears during a turn can cause a sudden change in power, which may cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before you ride. Even small problems are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means the motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of the lane.
Ride on the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The road is very slippery when rain first starts because water mixes with oil from cars. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you for better traction.

questions.question: Where is the greatest danger of conflict with other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: The biggest danger is at intersections. Oncoming cars turning left in front of motorcyclists cause the most conflicts.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle collisions.

options.text: Honking your horn at the wrong time

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgating
questions.explanation: Following too closely (tailgating) is a major cause of motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance from the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and turn your head to check blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and turn your head to check blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check blind spots in addition to using your mirrors before changing lanes.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop faster and more safely.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake and only use the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while stopping, release the front brake right away and then apply it firmly again. Use both brakes for quick stops.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to look.
Stop at the stop line and proceed through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line first. Then move forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to see if traffic is coming. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided into separate directions.

questions.question: How fast does your body remove alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour. This varies by person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Why is stopping difficult while turning?

options.text: There is less grip available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
The rider is focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use the brakes while turning, but only with care. When your motorcycle leans, some grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for stopping.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:
questions.correctAnswerText: Decreases.
questions.explanation: Your ability to ride safely gets worse as you drink more alcohol. If you have consumed any amount of alcohol, do not ride your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance for night riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead when riding at night.
